quiz.q: What are the two main benefits of JMS messaging stressed in class?
options: Lower licence cost and faster DataWeave
quiz.explain: The producer and consumer have no direct connection (decoupling), and the producer sends and forgets (asynchronous).

quiz.q: A new customer in Salesforce must be created in SAP, a database and a microservice. Which destination fits?
quiz.explain: A topic is one-to-many — every subscriber gets the same message. A queue is point-to-point.

quiz.q: In a queue, what happens to a message after a consumer receives and acknowledges it?
options: Every other consumer also gets it
quiz.explain: A queue is point-to-point; once consumed and acknowledged, the message is dequeued and can't be consumed again.

quiz.q: In Mule, where do JMS message headers and body end up?
quiz.explain: Like HTTP, JMS headers become attributes and the body becomes the payload.

quiz.q: Which JMS operation is a source that triggers the flow as soon as a message arrives?
quiz.explain: On New Message (named Listener in some Studio versions) is the source; Consume is a processor that takes a message only when the flow reaches it.

quiz.q: Which operation publishes a message and waits for the reply?
quiz.explain: Publish is asynchronous; Publish Consume is synchronous and waits for the response.

quiz.q: What is the Broker URL for a local ActiveMQ in the class JMS config?
quiz.explain: 61616 is the openwire transport connector; 8161 is the web console.

quiz.q: You publish to a queue name that doesn't exist yet in ActiveMQ. What happens?
options: The message is sent to a topic
The publish waits until the queue is created
quiz.explain: ActiveMQ auto-creates any queue you publish to; Anypoint MQ returns "destination not found". Use exact names.

quiz.q: With the default acknowledgement mode, when is a message acknowledged?
options: As soon as it is received
Only when the Ack operation runs
Never — it is deleted after 7 days
quiz.explain: AUTO is the default and acknowledges when the flow succeeds. IMMEDIATE acks on receipt; MANUAL waits for Ack.

quiz.q: With MANUAL acknowledgement, what do you pass to the Ack operation?
quiz.explain: Each message has an acknowledgement ID in `attributes.ackId`; the message stays pending until Ack runs.

quiz.q: A consumed message arrives as a String containing JSON, and `payload.name` doesn't work. What do you use?
quiz.explain: `read` converts a string/binary into its underlying format; `write` does the reverse.

quiz.q: App 1 must publish a message that app 2 consumes. Why won't the VM connector work?
options: VM queues are intra-app — they work only within the same application
quiz.explain: VM is for asynchronous communication within one application; JMS brokers and Anypoint MQ are inter-app.

cards.back: **Java Messaging Service** — a generic concept for communication between systems in a message format, with many brokers.
Apache ActiveMQ (open source, used in class), RabbitMQ, Apache Kafka, IBM MQ, and Anypoint MQ (MuleSoft's own, licensed, cloud-only).
To decouple systems and communicate asynchronously — the producer doesn't wait, consumers process independently, and messages survive while a downstream system is down.
A queue is **point-to-point** — one consumer, then removed. A topic is **one-to-many** — every subscriber gets the same message.
Headers → **attributes**, body → **payload**.
Publish is asynchronous — send and move on. Publish Consume is synchronous — it publishes and waits for the reply.
Consume is a processor that takes a message when the flow reaches it. On New Message is a source that triggers the flow when a message arrives.
Publish, Consume, On New Message (source), Publish Consume, Ack, Recover Session.
Telling the broker "I have successfully processed it", so the message is dequeued.
**AUTO** (default — when the flow succeeds), **IMMEDIATE** (on receipt), **DUPS_OK** (like AUTO, duplicates possible), **MANUAL** (Ack operation with `attributes.ackId`).
For long processes — acknowledge only near the end with the Ack operation and `#[attributes.ackId]`.
Messages that came in / were removed / are waiting. 10 enqueued, 5 dequeued → 5 pending.

cards.front: Purge vs. Delete in the ActiveMQ console
cards.back: Purge deletes the messages; Delete deletes the queue.
Broker (openwire) `tcp://localhost:61616`; web console `http://localhost:8161`.

cards.front: What do you need from the messaging team?
cards.back: Broker URL, username and password, and the queue/topic names (they create them).
ActiveMQ creates it automatically; Anypoint MQ returns "destination not found".
**Forever** — it's a source.
`read(s, "application/json")` turns a string/binary into structured data; `write(obj, "application/json")` turns it into a string.
Dead-letter queue for failed messages.
VM queues work only within one application (**intra-app**); JMS brokers and Anypoint MQ work between applications (**inter-app**).
MuleSoft's queuing service — an extra licence, for cloud-based deployments only.
CloudHub logs are limited or deleted within 30 days; send logs to queues and let a system like the ELK stack consume and store them.
